target_customer: Companies deploying agentic AI who need liability cover and proof of safety for enterprise procurement
problem: Traditional E&O and cyber policies exclude AI agent claims, so companies shipping agents have no coverage and no third party proof that an agent is safe.
business_model: Insurance premiums plus certification and financial guarantee fees, self-serve; website lists pricing from about $22,200 per year for early-stage AI products
product_category: AI agent liability insurance and certification

founders.name: Ines Boutemadja
founders.background_notes: YC page says she built insurance products and carrier infrastructure at SafetyWing (W18) and structured a Tokio Marine MGA.

founders.name: Julien Catonnet
founders.background_notes: YC page and company site describe corporate strategy consulting, then software engineering at VC-backed startups and enterprise compliance work. Employers not named.

competitors.name: AIUC
competitors.what: Standards, audits and insurance under AIUC-1 certification for AI agents

competitors.name: Mount
competitors.what: AI-native carrier with liability coverage for deployed agents

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly insurance structuring and risk evaluation (eight risk dimensions scored per the site) plus a testing playground; the hard parts are carrier partnerships and underwriting, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Insurance relationships and certification brand take time, but several startups were already selling similar AI cover in 2026 and the product is mostly packaging of underwriting.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per the company, existing policies carve out AI claims as of 2026; no incumbent copy is documented yet.

market_need_then: The company cites California AB 316 holding deployers liable, the EU AI Act enforcement in August, and insurers excluding AI claims; enterprise legal teams ask who pays when an agent fails.

branding.domain_note: Uses klaimee.ai, not a .com; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, plain-spoken copy with short headings and concrete examples (company site).

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch coverage and funding press found; no sources on brand recognition. Name is a claim pun, memorable but easy to misspell. A different Paris company also uses the name Klaimee, which creates confusion risk.

outcome_analysis: Klaimee is a young company that announced a $5.5M seed in July 2026, a few months after its Spring 2026 YC batch. Its CEO has direct insurance product experience from SafetyWing, and regulation and carve-outs in existing policies give it timing support. No outcome exists yet, and competitors AIUC, Armilla and Mount are in the same space.
notes: Seed confirmed by company site ($5.5M) and fintech.global; coverage lists investors consistently. One tracker lists $6M total and NeuronFeed says founded 2025 with $500K, both unverified and not used. A Dealroom entry klaimee_1 is a separate Paris health insurance company. Competitor list comes from an aggregator profile, undated beyond 2026.
